hlni.insight: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, how it is assessed, or what feedback you receive; these must be investigated as separate variables.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume a degree title dictates the exact work they will produce daily.
hlni.viewerChange: Replaces vague degree-title assumptions with a method for extracting concrete expectations.
hlni.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
hlni.payoff: The student uses the unanswered cells to define the exact question they need to ask the institution before choosing.

creativeAngle: Moving from degree-title assumptions to a concrete assessment-inquiry method.
objective: Enable students to evaluate B.Com and BBA by questioning specific task-assessment-feedback structures.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Assumption
shots.visual: A student sits at a desk with a notebook, writing 'B.Com' and 'BBA' at the top of two separate pages.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA? Don't just look at subject titles. They often overlap.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up of hands writing on paper, then panning to student's thoughtful face.

shots.name: The Method
shots.visual: Student draws a three-column table. Writes 'Example: Task: Analyze Sales Data. Assessment: ? Feedback: ?'
shots.dialogue: Try this audit. For any course, list the task, the assessment criteria, and the feedback type. If you have question marks, you have a gap.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze Sales Data. Assessment: ? Feedback: ?
shots.cameraPerformance: Top-down shot of the pen filling the columns clearly.

shots.name: The Resolution
shots.visual: Student circles the question marks and looks directly into the camera.
shots.dialogue: Now, ask: What specific task is evaluated in this module? That question guides your actual decision.
shots.onscreenText: What specific task is evaluated in this module?
shots.cameraPerformance: Steady, focused shot on the student.

productionNotes.camera: Stable tripod shots with close-ups on the writing
productionNotes.editing: Smooth transitions, focus on text readability
productionNotes.sound: Minimal ambient room tone, clear voiceover

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a structured three-column audit to force students to move past vague degree labels and identify missing information about how they will be assessed.

selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a degree title dictates the exact work they will produce daily.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Replaces vague degree-title assumptions with a method for extracting concrete expectations.
selected.concept: A student compares their expectations of 'B.Com' vs 'BBA' by drafting a three-column inquiry sheet.
selected.device: A split-screen showing a student filling out a physical worksheet to identify missing information.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: Student lists 'Marketing' for both B.Com and BBA and creates a three-column audit.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze Sales Data. Assessment: ? Feedback: ?
demonstration.observation: Recognizing that knowing 'Marketing' is taught is insufficient without knowing the assessment format.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific task is evaluated in this module?

comparedWith.hlni: An appealing option and an available option are different questions. Unknown requirements should be recorded as checks rather than assumed to be satisfied.
comparedWith.device: A checklist overlay on the screen as the student speaks.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A fast-paced 'mind map' reveal of a student's research process.
